blocks.text: What “cheap hosting in Pakistan” actually means

content.text: Web hosting is bought online, so buying from anywhere in Pakistan — Lahore, Karachi, Islamabad or a small town — works exactly the same way: you choose a plan, register a domain, pay, and your website goes live. There is no city-only price and no need to visit an office. What does differ for a buyer in Pakistan is practical: paying in PKR without currency conversion, paying with the wallets you already use, getting support in your own hours, and knowing the full price — including renewal — before you pay.

One thing to be careful about: some pages promise a local data center without saying what that means. ZedgeHost makes no such claim — its VPS server locations are New Jersey, Los Angeles and Dallas, chosen at checkout. Server location matters less than the basics for most small websites. What matters most is that your visitors get a fast, working website, that your plan includes SSL and backups, and that you can reach support when something breaks. Judge a provider on those, not on where its office sits.

The table below shows ZedgeHost’s actual plan prices. Shared, WordPress and cloud plans are billed yearly; VPS plans are billed monthly, with a yearly option available at checkout. For a detailed breakdown of what each plan costs and why, see
how much web hosting costs in Pakistan

Within each type there are larger plans: shared and WordPress hosting go up to Rs 9,999 per year, cloud hosting up to Rs 24,999 per year, and VPS hosting up to Rs 4,999 per month. Every plan includes a free SSL certificate, free cPanel, daily backups, free website migration and 24/7 support, with a 30-day money-back guarantee. “Cheap” only helps if those are included in the price — a lower headline price with SSL, backups and migration added at checkout is not actually cheaper.

blocks.text: Who needs which plan in Pakistan

content.text: Pakistan’s hosting buyers are not one group. A shop owner, a freelancer, a student and an agency all need different things — find your need below, and each one maps to a different starting plan.
A small business usually needs a professional website: who you are, what you sell, your location and contact details, and a contact or enquiry form.
Shared hosting from Rs 1,499 per year

covers this comfortably. An email address on your own domain reads as more trustworthy to customers than a free mailbox, and a simple catalogue with photos lets buyers see your products without a phone call.
Bloggers, freelancers and students usually build on WordPress: a blog, a portfolio, or a small site for a client.
WordPress hosting from Rs 1,499 per year
suits this, with one-click installs and the same included extras. If the site grows into heavy traffic or many posts and pages,
cloud hosting from Rs 9,999 per year
gives more room before you need a server of your own.
A small online store — products, prices, photos and an order form — runs fine on shared or WordPress hosting to start with. When orders and traffic grow, or when you host several websites,
VPS hosting from Rs 1,699 per month
gives dedicated resources and full server control, with a choice of server location (New Jersey, Los Angeles or Dallas) and operating system (AlmaLinux, Ubuntu, Debian, or an empty disk) at checkout.

Agencies and developers hosting several client websites at once usually land on VPS hosting, because each client site gets dedicated resources and the agency keeps full control of the server. Start with the smallest VPS plan and scale up only when the sites you host demand it.

blocks.text: A .pk domain for a Pakistani business

content.text: A .pk domain is not required, but it signals a Pakistani business and suits brands whose customers are mainly in Pakistan. Businesses dealing with customers outside Pakistan usually prefer a .com, which international customers recognise instantly. You can
search and register a domain
, including .pk and .com extensions, and point it at your hosting. For the registration steps, see
how to register a .pk domain in Pakistan

blocks.text: Paying in Pakistan: JazzCash, Easypaisa, Raast and bank transfer

content.text: ZedgeHost bills in PKR and accepts Easypaisa, JazzCash, Raast and bank transfer, so there are no currency conversion surprises and no need for an international credit card. That is the single most practical difference between a provider set up for Pakistani buyers and one that bills in dollars: the price you see is the price you pay, in rupees — whether you pay from a shop’s accounts or a student’s mobile wallet.

blocks.text: How to choose in five steps

items.text: One small website, catalogue or business site fits shared or WordPress hosting. A growing store, several websites or full server control points toward cloud or VPS.
Check the full price, not the headline.
Confirm the renewal price, whether SSL is included, and whether backups, cPanel and migration are in the plan or added at checkout.
Make sure you can pay in PKR with Easypaisa, JazzCash, Raast or bank transfer, without an international card or conversion fee.
Check support before you need it.
Note the support hours and contact options. ZedgeHost includes 24/7 support — test that you can actually reach a provider before your website depends on it.
A 30-day money-back guarantee means you can try the service and leave if it does not fit. Read the guarantee terms before you pay, with any provider.
